verdicts.served: PyKeePassGate can implement this today, over routes the gate already serves.
verdicts.needs-routes: Nothing in the design forbids it; the gate does not serve it yet.
verdicts.refused: Cannot exist on this side: it needs the file, the key, the XML document, or an operation the design refuses.

attachments: one GET per entry, so a database wide sweep is O(entries)
find_entries: built on the listing and the read routes
find_entries_by_username: needs a read per candidate, so it costs list plus N
trash_entry: DELETE already honors the recycle bin, but the gate does not expose trash and delete as two operations
recyclebin_group: the gate could name it and does not
save: the trap this whole question is about: it writes the file it was opened from
password: the client never holds the master password, which is the point of the gate
xml: there is no XML document on this side
deref: resolving a reference reads other entries, which the ACL may refuse, so a resolved value would be a permission decision made invisibly
move_entry: one operation about two nodes, and the router authorizes one. API.md records the refusal
empty_group: recursive delete, refused so that one grant cannot destroy entries nobody decided about
binaries: a database wide binary pool has no node for the ACL to authorize against
credchange_date: key change policy, which lives with the file
